html:
The vast palace that Nero built in the heart of Rome on land cleared by the Great Fire of 64 CE. Its name means "Golden House".

It was less a building than a landscape: pavilions, gardens, vineyards and woods spread over parts of three hills, with an artificial lake where the Colosseum now stands. In the entrance hall stood a bronze statue of Nero about thirty metres high, the Colossus of Nero. Inside were gilded rooms, painted walls and ceilings set with ivory. One octagonal hall, roofed with a concrete dome, survives. Nero is said to have remarked that at last he could live like a human being.

Romans hated it as a symbol of a tyrant who had taken their city for his park. After his death Vespasian drained the lake to build the Colosseum, and later emperors built baths over the rest. The rooms were buried and forgotten.

Around 1480 people found them underground and lowered themselves in. Artists such as Raphael copied the wall paintings. Because they seemed to be in caves, grottoes, the style was called "grotesque".
sum: The vast palace that Nero built in the heart of Rome on land cleared by the Great Fire of 64 CE. Its name means "Golden House".
